sats.label: SCISAT
sats.desc: Canada's 150 kg SCISAT has measured the chemistry of the ozone layer since 2003, with a special focus on Canada and the Arctic (CSA).
sats.source: Orbit source: CelesTrak public two-line elements for NORAD 27858 (SCISAT 1), propagated in the browser with satellite.js. A copy saved on 2026-11-09 is used if CelesTrak does not answer.
sats.alt: SCISAT — photo of the spacecraft. VANDENBERG AIR FORCE BASE, CALIF.-  A covered SciSat-1 spacecraft sits on a test stand at Vandenberg Air Force Base, Calif.  The solar arrays will be attached and the communications systems checked out.   The SciSat-1 weighs approximately 330 pounds and after launch will be placed in a 400-mile-high polar orbit to investigate processes that control the distribution of ozone in the upper atmosphere. The data from the satellite will provide Canadian and international scientists with improved measurements relating to global ozone processes and help policymakers assess existing environmental policy and develop protective measures for improving the health of our atmosphere, preventing further ozone depletion. The mission is designed to last two years.

sats.label: Sentinel-4 on MTG-S1
sats.desc: From geostationary orbit on MTG-S1, Sentinel-4 measures air pollution such as nitrogen dioxide and ozone over Europe and North Africa every hour (ESA).
sats.source: Orbit source: CelesTrak public two-line elements for NORAD 64723 (MTG-S1), propagated in the browser with satellite.js. A copy saved on 2026-11-09 is used if CelesTrak does not answer. Sentinel-4 is an instrument on the geostationary MTG-S1 weather satellite (NORAD 64723).
sats.alt: Sentinel-4 on MTG-S1 — photo of the spacecraft. Sentinel-4 on MTG-S ESA24700249.jpeg
sats.credit: Photo: ESA/Mlabspace, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0 igo).
sats.creditHtml: Photo: ESA/Mlabspace, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0 igo). Source

sats.label: MEV-2
sats.desc: Life extension in GEO: two MEVs have docked with three satellites, and the Mission Robotic Vehicle and three pods launched July 21, 2026 (company figures).
sats.source: Orbit source: CelesTrak public two-line elements for NORAD 46113 (MEV-2), propagated in the browser with satellite.js. A copy saved on 2026-11-09 is used if CelesTrak does not answer. MEV-2 stands in for Northrop Grumman SpaceLogistics life-extension vehicles in geostationary orbit.
sats.alt: MEV-2 — rendering of the spacecraft. Mev render.jpg
sats.credit: Rendering: NASA, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain).
sats.creditHtml: Rendering: NASA, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain). Source

sats.label: MetOp-SG-A1
sats.desc: Launched August 2025 on Ariane 6, MetOp-SG-A1 carries Sentinel-5, which delivers daily global data on air pollutants, ozone and climate gases.
sats.source: Orbit source: CelesTrak public two-line elements for NORAD 65159 (METOP-SGA1), propagated in the browser with satellite.js. A copy saved on 2026-11-09 is used if CelesTrak does not answer.
sats.alt: MetOp-SG-A1 — photo of the spacecraft. MetOp-SG-A satellite from below ESA511183.jpg
sats.credit: Photo: European Space Agency, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0 igo).
sats.creditHtml: Photo: European Space Agency, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0 igo). Source

sats.label: Aeolus
sats.desc: ESA guided its retired Aeolus wind satellite down in the first assisted reentry of its kind, cutting the already low debris risk by a factor of 150.
sats.source: Approximate sun-synchronous orbit near 320 km. Aeolus reentered on 28 July 2023, so there is no current TLE. The solution page describes the assisted reentry.
sats.alt: Aeolus — photo of the spacecraft. ADM-Aeolus model.jpg
sats.credit: Photo: SkywalkerPL, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0).
sats.creditHtml: Photo: SkywalkerPL, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0). Source

sats.label: DSCOVR
sats.desc: A camera photographing the entire sunlit face of Earth several times a day.
sats.source: Approximate. DSCOVR sits in a halo orbit around Sun–Earth L1, about 1.5 million km toward the Sun (NASA/NOAA). It is drawn much closer so Earth stays visible. A standard Earth TLE is not used.
sats.alt: DSCOVR — rendering of the spacecraft. Deep Space Climate Observatory (DSCOVR).jpg
sats.credit: Rendering: NASA, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain).
sats.creditHtml: Rendering: NASA, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain). Source

sats.label: Aditya-L1
sats.desc: Aditya-L1 is ISRO's first space-based solar observatory, studying the Sun from a halo orbit around L1, about 1.5 million km from Earth.
sats.source: Approximate. Aditya-L1 studies the Sun from a halo orbit around Sun–Earth L1, about 1.5 million km from Earth (solution page). Drawn closer than the real distance.
sats.alt: Aditya-L1 — photo of the spacecraft. Aditya-L1 spacecraft.jpg
sats.credit: Photo: Indian Space Research Organisation, via Wikimedia Commons (GODL-India).
sats.creditHtml: Photo: Indian Space Research Organisation, via Wikimedia Commons (GODL-India). Source

sats.label: SOHO
sats.pageName: SOHO Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (ESA / NASA)
sats.desc: Watching the Sun nonstop since 1995, SOHO helps experts predict solar storms and has found more than 5,000 comets (NASA).
sats.source: Approximate. SOHO has watched the Sun from Sun–Earth L1 since 1995 (solution page). Drawn closer than the real distance. A standard Earth TLE is not used.
sats.alt: SOHO — photo of the spacecraft. NASA SOHO spacecraft.png
sats.credit: Photo: Cgruda, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain).
sats.creditHtml: Photo: Cgruda, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain). Source

sats.label: IMAP
sats.desc: NASA's IMAP watches the Sun from about a million miles sunward and can give about a half hour's warning of incoming radiation.
sats.source: Approximate. IMAP watches the Sun from about a million miles sunward, around Sun–Earth L1 (solution page). No standard Earth TLE named IMAP was found on 9 November 2026. Drawn closer than the real distance.
sats.alt: IMAP — photo of the spacecraft. IMAP Rollout for Launch
sats.credit: Image: NASA (IMAP Rollout for Launch).
sats.creditHtml: Image: NASA (IMAP Rollout for Launch). Source

sats.label: Carruthers
sats.desc: The first mission dedicated to Earth's exosphere, Carruthers watches our planet's ultraviolet halo from about a million miles sunward.
sats.source: Approximate. The solution page says Carruthers watches Earth’s exosphere from about a million miles sunward (Sun–Earth L1). Drawn closer than the real distance.
sats.alt: Carruthers — photo of the spacecraft. Carruthers Geocorona Observatory Images (SVS14830 - 24-22101-Carruthers SpaceVehicleComplete-Edited).jpg
sats.credit: Photo: NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio - eMITS/Beth Anthony, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain).
sats.creditHtml: Photo: NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio - eMITS/Beth Anthony, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain). Source

sats.label: James Webb
sats.desc: How the James Webb Space Telescope tracked asteroid 2024 YR4 in February 2026 and ruled out a 2032 Moon impact, two years before ground telescopes could.
sats.source: Approximate. The James Webb Space Telescope operates around Sun–Earth L2 (NASA). This solution page is about Webb’s look at asteroid 2024 YR4. Drawn closer than the real distance.
sats.alt: James Webb — photo of the spacecraft. James Webb Space Telescope Mirror37.jpg
sats.credit: Photo: NASA/MSFC/David Higginbotham/Emmett Given, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain).
sats.creditHtml: Photo: NASA/MSFC/David Higginbotham/Emmett Given, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain). Source

sats.label: NEO Surveyor
sats.desc: NASA NEO Surveyor is the first space telescope built to find hazardous asteroids, including dark ones hidden in the Sun's glare. Launch NET September 2027.
sats.source: Approximate. NEO Surveyor is planned for a halo orbit around Sun–Earth L1 and has not launched (solution page). Drawn closer than the real distance.
sats.alt: NEO Surveyor — photo of the spacecraft. NEO Surveyor’s Telescope Gets Mounted to Its Flight Base
sats.credit: Image: NASA (NEO Surveyor’s Telescope Gets Mounted to Its Flight Base).
sats.creditHtml: Image: NASA (NEO Surveyor’s Telescope Gets Mounted to Its Flight Base). Source
sats.imageTitle: NEO Surveyor’s Telescope Gets Mounted to Its Flight Base

sats.label: GeoXO
sats.desc: NOAA's next generation of geostationary weather satellites, planned from 2032, will improve warnings of severe weather and hazards (NOAA).
sats.source: Approximate geostationary orbit. GeoXO is a future NOAA/NASA series and is not in orbit yet (solution page). The longitude is a placeholder.
sats.alt: GeoXO — rendering of the spacecraft. NASA Awards Contracts for NOAA GeoXO Spacecraft Phase A Study (NESDIS 2022-07-26).jpg
sats.credit: Rendering: NOAA, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain).
sats.creditHtml: Rendering: NOAA, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain). Source
sats.imageTitle: File:NASA Awards Contracts for NOAA GeoXO Spacecraft Phase A Study (NESDIS 2022-07-26).jpg

sats.label: LignoSat
sats.desc: LignoSat, the world's first wooden satellite, proved wood can survive in orbit; a follow-on is a potential solution on the horizon.
sats.source: Approximate. LignoSat was deployed from the International Space Station into low Earth orbit (NASA, cited on the solution page). No current TLE named LignoSat was found on 9 November 2026, so it is drawn near the station’s orbit.
sats.alt: LignoSat — photo of the spacecraft. JAXA’s First Wooden Satellite Deploys from Space Station (iss072e352043).jpg
sats.credit: Photo: NASA, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain).
sats.creditHtml: Photo: NASA, via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain). Source
sats.imageTitle: File:JAXA’s First Wooden Satellite Deploys from Space Station (iss072e352043).jpg

sats.label: Starfish Otter
sats.desc: The first Otter launched October 1, 2026 for NASA's SSPICY mission, inspecting up to four dead satellites and rocket bodies from 2027.
sats.source: Approximate low Earth orbit. The solution page says the first Otter launched on 1 October 2026 on Transporter-18 to inspect objects in low Earth orbit. No CelesTrak entry named Starfish or SSPICY was found on 9 November 2026. The picture is Starfish’s Otter Pup, an earlier vehicle in the same Otter design.
sats.alt: Starfish Otter — rendering of the spacecraft. Starfish Space - Otter Pup.png
sats.credit: Rendering: Jmthompson2020, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0).
sats.creditHtml: Rendering: Jmthompson2020, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0). Source

skipped.why: They use satellite data, or watch satellites from the ground, but they are not one spacecraft in orbit.
Not Earth-observing or debris satellites. GEDI and EMIT, which ride on the station, are included.
They do not stay in Earth orbit or at Sun–Earth L1, L2, or L5.
